note: Venice acquired Ragusa under the Treaty of Zadar (1205) following the Fourth Crusade, maintaining overlordship until 1358 when the Treaty of Zadar (1358) transferred Ragusa to the Kingdom of Hungary-Croatia. Venetian rule gave Ragusa its commercial infrastructure (the Fondaco system, standardized weights and measures) but also subjected it to unfavorable trade restrictions. Ragusa's eventual break from Venice — achieved through Hungarian overlordship — gave it the greater commercial freedom that enabled its 15th-century golden age.

_quarry.structural_significance: Venetian overlordship shapes Ragusa's commercial infrastructure but restricts its autonomy; the shift to Hungarian overlordship (1358) gives Ragusa the freedom to develop its own merchant fleet and diplomatic network — the foundation of its later golden age
